q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A transfer entry adjusting charges between two work orders of the same workshop is an internal adjustment and does not pass through the Account Current.
2. Transactions between a workshop and another accounting unit of the railway are settled through the Account Current and not by cash payment.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Transfers within one workshop between its own work orders are internal adjustments, while work for another accounting unit is settled through the Account Current, not cash, under Workshop Accounts Code procedure. Hence both statements are correct.

q: In distributing the wages of workshop staff to jobs, the amount charged to the work orders is:

options.A: The net wages payable after deducting Provident Fund and other recoveries
options.B: The gross wages earned, the deductions from wages being credited to the respective heads and not treated as a reduction of the job cost
options.C: The wages net of income tax deduction only
options.D: The wages actually drawn in cash by the staff

e: Job cost must bear the gross wages earned on the job. Provident Fund and other deductions are recoveries credited to their respective heads, not a reduction of labour cost charged to the work order.

q: Where an outside body deposits the estimated cost of a work with the railway before the work is taken in hand in a workshop, the deposit is initially:

options.A: Credited to a deposit head, the expenditure being booked under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense and adjusted against the deposit on completion of the work
options.B: Credited directly to the revenue earnings of the workshop
options.C: Debited to Workshop Manufacturing Suspense as an advance to the workshop
options.D: Credited to the Stock Adjustment Account

e: Money deposited in advance by an outside body is first credited to a deposit head. Expenditure is booked under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense and adjusted against the deposit when the work is completed.

q: A workshop has raised transfer items in its Account Current for work done for another accounting unit, but the receiving unit has not accepted the items. Such unaccepted items are dealt with by:

options.A: Writing them off to shop on-cost at the end of the month
options.B: Cancelling the work orders on which the work was done
options.C: Recovering the amount in cash from the staff of the receiving unit
options.D: Keeping them outstanding in the transfer accounts and pursuing the receiving unit for acceptance and adjustment

e: Transfer items raised in the Account Current remain outstanding in the transfer accounts until the receiving unit accepts them. The executing workshop must pursue acceptance and adjustment; it cannot write them off or recover cash.

q: At the periodical review of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, apart from age-wise analysis, the outstanding items are also classified according to the reason for their pendency, so that it is brought out whether an item is outstanding because:

options.A: The worker who executed the job has been transferred
options.B: The stores depot has changed its issue rates
options.C: The job is still in progress, or its completion report or transfer entry is awaited, or acceptance of the indenting unit is awaited
options.D: The shop incharge has proceeded on leave

e: Review of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense classifies outstandings by reason for pendency - job in progress, completion report or transfer entry awaited, or acceptance awaited - besides age-wise analysis, so action can be targeted.

q: Material issued from the stores depot to workshop jobs is recorded quantity-wise in the depot's numerical account and value-wise in the priced stores ledger maintained by the Accounts office. The reconciliation between the two records is necessary in order to ensure that:

options.A: The outturn of the shops agrees with the POH programme
options.B: The quantities issued as per the depot agree in value with the amounts debited to the work orders
options.C: The wages of depot staff agree with the labour pay sheets
options.D: The balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense agrees with the Plant Register

e: The depot keeps quantities in its numerical account while Accounts keeps values in the priced stores ledger. Reconciliation ensures quantities issued agree in value with amounts debited to work orders.

q: The total cost of machinery and plant as recorded in the Plant Register of a workshop should agree with:

options.A: The corresponding balance in the Block Account (capital account) of the railway for workshop machinery and plant
options.B: The balance under Stores Suspense of the railway
options.C: The total of the on-cost folios of the shops
options.D: The value of work-in-progress in the Workshop General Register

e: The Plant Register records workshop machinery and plant at cost. Its total must agree with the corresponding balance in the Block Account for workshop machinery and plant, proving the capital record.

q: Tools issued on loan to a workshop worker from the tool room are lost by him and, after due enquiry, the loss is held to be due to his negligence. The correct treatment is that:

options.A: The cost of the tools is charged to the job on which he was last working
options.B: The loss is ignored, as tools are consumable stores
options.C: The tools are replaced from the imprest cash of the shop
options.D: The cost of the lost tools is recovered from the worker, or written off under competent sanction where recovery is not enforced, and his tool loan account is adjusted accordingly

e: Tools lost through a worker's negligence are charged to him after enquiry, or written off under competent sanction if recovery is not enforced. His tool loan account is then adjusted to clear the outstanding tool.

q: Serviceable components released from rolling stock and reconditioned in a workshop for further use are taken into stores stock:

options.A: At the price of a new component
options.B: At a nominal value of one rupee in all cases
options.C: At their assessed value, which is lower than the cost of a new component, the job from which they were released being credited accordingly
options.D: At the original cost at which they were first issued

e: Serviceable released components reconditioned for reuse are taken into stock at their assessed value, below new cost, reflecting their remaining service value. The releasing job is credited with that assessed value.

q: A canteen for workshop staff is run departmentally in a workshop. The net cost of running the canteen, after taking credit for its receipts, is borne in workshop costing as:

options.A: A direct charge on the jobs executed during meal breaks
options.B: General on-cost of the workshop, being a staff welfare expense
options.C: Proforma on-cost of the workshop
options.D: A deduction from the wages of the staff using the canteen

e: A departmental canteen's net cost, after its receipts, is a staff welfare expense not identifiable with any job. It is therefore borne as general on-cost of the workshop as a whole.

q: Casual labour is engaged on muster rolls specifically for the erection of a new machine sanctioned as a capital work in a workshop. The wages of this casual labour are:

options.A: Charged directly to that capital job, being booked through the muster rolls for the specific work
options.B: Charged to shop on-cost of the shop in which the machine is erected
options.C: Charged to the revenue standing work order of the shop
options.D: Debited to Workshop Manufacturing Suspense as a manufacture job

e: Casual labour engaged specifically for a sanctioned capital work, here erection of a new machine, is charged directly to that capital job through its muster rolls, since the labour is wholly identifiable with that work.

q: Wages of workshop staff which remain undisbursed are held under the Unpaid Wages head. Amounts which still remain unclaimed after the prescribed period and due notice are finally:

options.A: Distributed among the staff of the shop concerned
options.B: Transferred to the Staff Benefit Fund automatically
options.C: Held under the head permanently, without any limit of time
options.D: Credited to the revenue of the railway

e: Undisbursed wages are held under Unpaid Wages. Amounts still unclaimed after the prescribed period and due notice are finally credited to railway revenue, as no claimant remains entitled to them.

q: The bill raised by a workshop against another railway for Periodic Overhaul of that railway's rolling stock is built up of:

options.A: Material cost only, labour being borne by the home railway
options.B: A fixed hire charge per day of detention of the stock
options.C: Labour, material, on-cost and the prescribed proforma and departmental charges applicable to foreign work
options.D: The market price of a similar overhaul in the trade

e: A bill for Periodic Overhaul of another railway's stock must recover its full cost: labour, material and on-cost, plus the prescribed proforma and departmental charges applicable to foreign work.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where outlay is booked on a workshop job in one financial year but the outturn is transferred out in the next year, the final head (Revenue or Capital) is debited in the year in which the outturn is transferred.
2. The final head of a workshop job is debited in the year in which the first item of outlay is booked on the job, irrespective of when the outturn is transferred.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The final Revenue or Capital head is debited when the outturn is transferred out of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, even if outlay began in an earlier year. Hence statement 1 alone is correct.

q: On-cost standing work orders of a shop differ from manufacture work orders in that the on-cost standing work orders:

options.A: Are opened only for capital jobs of the shop
options.B: Are period accounts, closed month by month after the on-cost collected under them is distributed over the jobs of the period
options.C: Remain open until a particular article is completed
options.D: Are maintained by the stores depot attached to the workshop

e: On-cost standing work orders are period accounts. On-cost collected under them during a month is distributed over that period's jobs and the standing orders are closed month by month, unlike manufacture orders closed on completion.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Departmental charges are not levied in addition to cost on work done by a workshop for its own railway.
2. Departmental charges are levied in addition to cost on work done by a workshop for another Government department or an outside body.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Departmental charges are an addition over cost only for work done for another Government department or outside body. No such charge is levied on work done for the workshop's own railway. Both statements are correct.

q: During a month, a workshop worker is employed partly on measured jobs under the incentive scheme and partly on unmeasured day work for which no allowed time exists. His incentive bonus for the month is:

options.A: Computed on the whole of his attendance time for the month
options.B: Paid at the average rate of the shop on the unmeasured work also
options.C: Not payable at all for that month
options.D: Payable only in respect of the time saved by him on the measured jobs, the unmeasured time being paid at the time rate only

e: Incentive bonus is payable only for time saved against allowed time on measured jobs. Time on unmeasured day work has no allowed time, so it is paid at the time rate only, with no bonus.

q: A workshop executes a repair job for a sister workshop of the same railway which is a separate accounting unit. On completion, the cost of the job is recovered from the sister workshop:

options.A: Through a transfer transaction in the Account Current between the two accounting units
options.B: In cash, through the cash office of the executing workshop
options.C: By debiting the cost finally to the revenue head of the executing workshop
options.D: By adjustment against the wages bill of the sister workshop

e: A sister workshop that is a separate accounting unit settles through a transfer transaction in the Account Current. Cash payment or debit to the executing workshop's own revenue head would be incorrect.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The cost of a new machine purchased under the Machinery and Plant Programme, together with its installation charges, accumulates under the capital head until the machine is installed and commissioned.
2. Depreciation of such a machine is charged to shop on-cost from the date of its purchase, even before it is installed and put to use.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Cost of a Machinery and Plant Programme machine plus installation accumulates under Capital until commissioning. Depreciation, a charge for use, begins only after installation, not from purchase. Hence statement 1 alone is correct.

q: A workshop store holds 100 units of a material valued at Rs 10 per unit and receives a fresh consignment of 200 units at Rs 13 per unit. Under the weighted average method, the value of an issue of 150 units made thereafter is:
e: Weighted average rate is (100 x Rs 10 + 200 x Rs 13) / 300 = Rs 3,600 / 300 = Rs 12 per unit. Issue of 150 units is therefore 150 x Rs 12 = Rs 1,800.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Scrap arising on a workshop job is credited to the job at its assessed value when it is returned to the stores depot.
2. The difference between the amount actually realised on the sale of such scrap and the value at which it was taken into stock is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Scrap returned to stores is credited to the job at assessed value. Any difference between that stock value and the amount actually realised on sale is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account. Both statements are correct.

q: The incentive bonus paid to essential indirect workers of a shop, which is linked to the average bonus of the direct workers, is accounted for in workshop costing as:

options.A: A direct labour charge on the jobs done by the direct workers
options.B: A charge to the Capital head of the workshop
options.C: A recovery from the direct workers of the shop
options.D: Part of the shop on-cost, since the indirect workers are not booked to individual jobs

e: Essential indirect workers are not booked to individual jobs, so even bonus linked to direct workers' average bonus forms part of shop on-cost, which is then absorbed over jobs of the shop.

q: Staff specially maintained in a workshop as a leave reserve, to relieve workers proceeding on leave, are not booked to individual jobs. Their pay is charged to:

options.A: On-cost
options.B: The jobs on which the workers relieved by them were last engaged
options.C: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense as direct labour
options.D: The Pension Fund

e: Leave reserve staff relieve others and are not booked to individual jobs. Their pay is an indirect labour cost and is therefore charged to on-cost.

q: Ordinary repairs to the buildings of a workshop are not booked under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense because such repairs:

options.A: Are executed free of cost by the workshop staff themselves
options.B: Are the responsibility of the Engineering department and are charged to the revenue head for repairs of buildings
options.C: Are charged to the Capital head in all cases
options.D: Are met from the imprest cash of the Chief Workshop Manager

e: Ordinary repairs to workshop buildings are the Engineering department's responsibility and are charged to the revenue head for building repairs, not booked under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense.

q: A workshop executes a job for another Government department. The cost booked on the job is: material Rs 45,000, labour Rs 30,000 and on-cost Rs 15,000. Departmental charges recoverable on the work amount to Rs 10,000. The amount of the bill to be raised against the department is:
e: Bill equals material Rs 45,000 + labour Rs 30,000 + on-cost Rs 15,000 = Rs 90,000, plus departmental charges Rs 10,000 for work for another Government department, giving Rs 1,00,000.

q: At the close of a period, a process shop of a workshop has partly finished work lying in the process on which material of Rs 30,000, labour of Rs 20,000 and on-cost of Rs 10,000 have been booked. The value of the work-in-progress of the process for the period is:
e: Work-in-progress of a process shop is valued at all cost booked on the partly finished work: material Rs 30,000 + labour Rs 20,000 + on-cost Rs 10,000 = Rs 60,000.

q: Where a workshop runs its own power house, the cost per unit of electricity generated for distribution among the shops is arrived at by dividing:

options.A: The total cost of running the power house for a period by the number of units of electricity generated in that period
options.B: The cost of the power house building by its expected life
options.C: The total wages of the workshop by the units generated
options.D: The cost of coal stocked in the workshop by the units generated

e: Unit cost of power is total cost of running the power house for a period divided by units generated in that period. This rate is then used to charge consuming shops.

q: Components manufactured in a workshop for use as tools and plant of the workshop itself are, on completion, dealt with by:

options.A: Taking them into stores stock as ordinary stores items
options.B: Transferring their cost out of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense to the Tools and Plant head of the workshop
options.C: Writing off their cost to shop on-cost
options.D: Selling them and purchasing similar tools from the market

e: Components made for the workshop's own tools and plant are capital-type assets of the workshop. On completion their cost is transferred out of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense to the Tools and Plant head.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Before a work order is finally closed, it is ensured that all surplus material drawn for the job has been returned to stores and credited to the job.
2. Before a work order is finally closed, it is also ensured that serviceable released material and scrap arising on the job have been returned and credited to the job.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Before closure, a work order must get credit for all surplus material returned, and for serviceable released material and scrap returned to stores. Both checks ensure the job bears only its net cost.

q: The job cards and tally sheets rendered by the shops, after the labour distribution has been compiled from them, are retained in the Workshop Accounts Office mainly because they:

options.A: Are required for fixing the following year's POH programme
options.B: Are sent to the Railway Board along with the Account Current
options.C: Form the basis of the stores price ledger
options.D: Are the supporting vouchers for the labour booked to the work orders, available for internal check and audit

e: Job cards and tally sheets support the labour distribution compiled from them. They are retained in the Workshop Accounts Office as vouchers for labour booked to work orders, for internal check and audit.

q: Material requisitions drawn by shops against work orders show quantities only. The pricing of such requisitions, at the stores issue rates, for debit to the work orders is done by:

options.A: The Accounts office, from the priced stores ledger
options.B: The chargeman of the shop drawing the material
options.C: The Production Control Organisation
options.D: The cash office of the workshop

e: Shops draw material by quantity-only requisitions. Pricing at stores issue rates for debit to work orders is done by the Accounts office from the priced stores ledger, which alone carries values.

q: During verification of the material lying in a shop, a shortage is found against the quantities drawn for jobs and not yet accounted for. Pending investigation, the value of the shortage is:

options.A: Credited to the work order last executed in the shop
options.B: Written off at once to the Pension Fund
options.C: Held under objection/suspense and, after investigation, adjusted under the orders of the competent authority
options.D: Recovered in equal shares from all workers of the shop without any enquiry

e: A shortage of shop material pending investigation is held under objection or suspense. After investigation it is adjusted under orders of the competent authority, not written off or recovered without enquiry.

q: A worn component of rolling stock can either be reclaimed in the workshop or replaced by a new component. The decision to reclaim is guided mainly by comparing:

options.A: The scrap value of the worn component with the price of a new one
options.B: The cost of reclamation, together with the further service life the reclaimed component will give, with the cost of a new component
options.C: The labour cost of reclamation alone with the material cost of a new component
options.D: The age of the worn component alone with its codal life

e: Reclamation is justified only if its cost, judged with the further service life it will give, compares favourably with the cost of a new component. Age or scrap value alone cannot decide the choice.

q: The amount realised on the sale of a condemned item of workshop machinery and plant, which was originally charged to Capital or the Depreciation Reserve Fund, is:

options.A: Credited to the revenue earnings of the workshop
options.B: Credited to shop on-cost of the shop which used the machine
options.C: Retained in the imprest cash of the workshop
options.D: Credited to the same Capital or Depreciation Reserve Fund head, in release of the capital cost of the asset

e: Sale proceeds of condemned machinery originally charged to Capital or Depreciation Reserve Fund are credited back to that same head, in release of the asset's capital cost, not treated as revenue earnings.

q: A workshop manufactures an article against the indent of the open line of its own railway, the article being required for direct use and not for stocking. On completion, the cost of the article is:

options.A: Transferred directly to the final Revenue or Capital head of the indenting open line unit, without the article passing through stores stock
options.B: Held permanently under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.C: Credited to the earnings of the workshop as a sale
options.D: Transferred to Stores Suspense in all cases

e: An article made for direct use of the indenting open line unit, not for stocking, is transferred straight to that unit's final Revenue or Capital head on completion, without passing through stores stock.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fixed on-cost of a workshop remains broadly constant in total over a period, irrespective of the volume of outturn in that period.
2. Variable on-cost varies in total broadly in proportion to the volume of outturn, remaining broadly constant per unit of outturn.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Fixed on-cost stays broadly constant in total regardless of outturn volume, while variable on-cost varies in total with outturn and stays broadly constant per unit. This is the standard cost behaviour distinction; both are correct.

q: The cost of Periodic Overhaul transferred out of a workshop to revenue is classified in the revenue accounts:

options.A: Under a single combined head for all rolling stock, without any break-up
options.B: By the class of stock overhauled, such as locomotives, carriages and wagons
options.C: By the name of the workshop which carried out the overhaul
options.D: By the trade of the staff employed on the overhaul

e: Periodic Overhaul cost transferred to revenue is classified by class of stock overhauled - locomotives, carriages and wagons - so revenue accounts show overhaul cost for each stock class separately.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Articles manufactured in a workshop but not yet transferred to the stores depot continue to form part of the balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense.
2. Such articles enter the stores stock account only when they are actually transferred to and taken over by the stores depot.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Manufactured articles not yet handed over remain part of the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense balance. They enter stores stock only when actually transferred to and taken over by the stores depot. Both statements are correct.

q: In the costing organisation of a workshop, the distinction between a cost centre and a cost unit is that:

options.A: The shop and the job are both cost units of the workshop
options.B: A shop or section, to which costs are allocated and from which they are absorbed, is a cost centre, whereas the job or work order, for which cost is ascertained, is the cost unit
options.C: A cost centre is maintained only in the stores depot
options.D: The cost unit of a workshop is always one tonne of outturn

e: A cost centre is a shop or section to which costs are allocated and from which they are absorbed. A cost unit is the job or work order for which cost is finally ascertained. The two terms are thus distinct.

q: The monthly outturn statement of a workshop shows physical outturn transferred by the shops in excess of the value transferred out in the accounts for the same month. The correct course for the Workshop Accounts Office is to:

options.A: Accept the statement as rendered, the difference being a normal feature
options.B: Charge the difference to shop on-cost
options.C: Reduce the following month's programme by the excess outturn
options.D: Investigate and reconcile the difference between the shops' outturn returns and the accounts transfers before the monthly accounts are closed

e: Physical outturn in shop returns must reconcile with value transferred out in accounts. Any excess must be investigated and reconciled by the Workshop Accounts Office before monthly accounts are closed.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where workshop staff are deputed to work in a workshop of another railway, the work on which they are employed is executed and its cost compiled in the workshop where the work is actually done.
2. The pay and allowances of staff so deputed are ultimately borne by the railway which takes their services, the adjustment being made through transfer transactions.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Cost of work is compiled where the work is actually done, even for deputed staff of another railway, and their pay is ultimately borne by the railway taking their services through transfer transactions. Both statements are correct.

q: The pay of the watch and ward (security) staff employed for guarding the workshop premises as a whole is treated in workshop costing as:

options.A: A direct charge on the jobs in progress at night
options.B: General on-cost of the workshop
options.C: Proforma on-cost of the workshop
options.D: A charge to the Capital head of the workshop

e: Watch and ward staff guard the workshop premises as a whole, not any particular job. Their pay is therefore general on-cost of the workshop.

q: New coaches manufactured in a railway workshop under the Rolling Stock Programme are, on completion and transfer of their cost out of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, charged to:

options.A: Capital under Plan Head 21 - Rolling Stock (or the Depreciation Reserve Fund, where provided as replacements)
options.B: Revenue working expenses of the workshop
options.C: Plan Head 72 - Manufacturing Suspense permanently
options.D: The Stores Suspense head

e: New coaches built under the Rolling Stock Programme are charged on completion to Capital under Plan Head 21 - Rolling Stock, or to the Depreciation Reserve Fund where they are provided as replacements.

q: A workshop takes up, as emergent work, the repair of rolling stock of another railway before the formal acceptance and work order of that railway are received. Until the acceptance is received and the bill can be raised, the cost booked on the work is:

options.A: Written off to the revenue of the executing workshop
options.B: Debited to the Staff Benefit Fund
options.C: Charged to shop on-cost of the shops which did the repair
options.D: Held under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense against the job, pending regularisation and recovery

e: Emergent repair of another railway's stock done before formal acceptance is held under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense against the job. It stays there pending regularisation, acceptance and recovery.

q: A clerk, in absorbing on-cost on a job, applies the shop on-cost percentage to the total of material, labour and direct expenses booked on the job. The error in this working is that on-cost in the workshop is absorbed:

options.A: On the material cost of the job only
options.B: On the total cost of the job including proforma charges
options.C: Equally on all jobs of the shop, irrespective of their size
options.D: On the direct labour charges of the job, direct expenses and material not forming part of the absorption base

e: Workshop on-cost is absorbed on the direct labour charges of a job only. Applying the percentage to material and direct expenses also inflates the base and over-absorbs on-cost on the job.

q: A workshop is manufacturing an article which is also available for purchase from the trade. In deciding whether manufacture in the workshop should be continued or the article should be bought out, the comparison is properly made between the market price and:

options.A: The prime cost of the article in the workshop
options.B: The full cost of the article in the workshop, including general and proforma on-cost, so that the comparison is on a like basis
options.C: The direct labour cost of the article in the workshop
options.D: The material cost of the article in the workshop

e: A make-or-buy decision must compare market price with the workshop's full cost, including general and proforma on-cost, so both sides are on a like basis. Prime or partial cost would understate workshop cost.

q: Standard components required regularly by the open line are manufactured in a workshop for stocking in the stores depot, without waiting for an indent against each lot. Such manufacture is undertaken:

options.A: Under the authorised stock manufacture programme of the workshop, the cost being transferred to stores stock on completion of each lot
options.B: Only after a sale bill has been raised on the stores depot
options.C: As shop on-cost work, since no indent exists
options.D: Only under the Rolling Stock Programme of the Railway Board

e: Regular stock manufacture for the depot is done under the authorised stock manufacture programme without waiting for an indent for each lot. Cost of each completed lot is transferred to stores stock.

q: The shop on-cost of a shop for a month is Rs 1,20,000 and the direct labour booked on jobs of the shop in the month is Rs 4,00,000. A job of the shop has direct labour of Rs 50,000. The shop on-cost absorbed on the job is:
e: Shop on-cost percentage is Rs 1,20,000 / Rs 4,00,000 = 30 per cent of direct labour. On direct labour of Rs 50,000, absorbed on-cost is 30 per cent x Rs 50,000 = Rs 15,000.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The cost accounts of a workshop are periodically reconciled with its financial accounts, so that the total cost compiled on jobs agrees with the expenditure recorded in the general books.
2. Differences noticed in such reconciliation are allowed to remain unadjusted, since the cost accounts are only memorandum records.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Cost accounts must be reconciled periodically with financial accounts so job costs agree with expenditure in the general books. Differences cannot be left unadjusted merely because cost records are memorandum; statement 1 alone is correct.

q: A worker is marked present in the gate attendance record of a workshop but is reported absent from his shop for the whole day, with no leave sanctioned and no other duty assigned to him. In compiling the labour pay sheet, the Workshop Accounts Office will:

options.A: Pay him for the day, since the gate record shows him present
options.B: Charge his wages for the day to shop on-cost
options.C: Recover the amount from the chargeman of the shop
options.D: Treat him as absent for the day and pay no wages for it, the gate record alone not being sufficient to establish his presence on duty

e: Gate attendance alone does not prove presence on duty. A worker reported absent from his shop all day, with no leave or other duty, is treated as absent and paid no wages for that day in the labour pay sheet.

q: A new operation is introduced in a shop and no allowed time has yet been fixed for it by work study. For the period until an allowed time is fixed, the workers employed on the operation are:

options.A: Paid incentive bonus at the average rate earned in the shop
options.B: Paid wages at the time rate only, incentive bonus becoming payable only for the time saved against an allowed time duly fixed
options.C: Paid bonus on the basis of the allowed time of a similar operation of another workshop, without any local fixation
options.D: Not paid any wages until the allowed time is fixed

e: Incentive bonus depends on time saved against an allowed time fixed by work study. Until an allowed time exists for a new operation, workers on it are paid at the time rate only.

q: An electroplating shop of a workshop does plating work for jobs of several other shops and does not itself produce a final article. The cost collected in the electroplating shop for a period is:

options.A: Written off to general on-cost of the workshop in all cases
options.B: Charged to the stores depot attached to the workshop
options.C: Distributed over the jobs for which plating was done, on the basis of the work performed for each job
options.D: Recovered in cash from the shops concerned

e: An electroplating shop is a service shop producing no final article. Its period cost is distributed over the jobs for which plating was actually done, on the basis of work performed for each job.

q: At the periodical physical verification of loose tools and plant held in a shop, certain tools recorded in the tools register are not forthcoming. The correct course is that:

options.A: The shortage is investigated and the cost is recovered from the person responsible, or written off under the sanction of the competent authority, and the tools register is adjusted accordingly
options.B: The register is rewritten without the missing tools, without any investigation
options.C: The cost of the missing tools is charged to the job in progress in the shop
options.D: The shortage is ignored, as loose tools are consumable stores

e: Tools missing at physical verification must be investigated. Cost is recovered from the person responsible or written off under competent sanction, and the tools register is adjusted accordingly.

q: During the progress of a manufacture job, it becomes clear that its cost will materially exceed the estimated cost on the basis of which the work order was sanctioned. The correct course is to:

options.A: Continue booking expenditure and close the job at whatever cost it reaches
options.B: Transfer the excess over the estimate to shop on-cost
options.C: Stop all work on the job permanently
options.D: Bring the expected excess to notice and obtain a revised estimate or the sanction of the competent authority for the excess, the Accounts office watching that expenditure does not proceed indefinitely beyond the sanctioned estimate

e: When cost will materially exceed the sanctioned estimate, the excess must be brought to notice and a revised estimate or competent sanction obtained. Accounts must watch that spending does not continue indefinitely beyond sanction.

q: On a workshop job, the prime cost is Rs 1,40,000, shop on-cost absorbed is Rs 35,000, general on-cost is Rs 15,000 and proforma on-cost is Rs 10,000. The full cost of the job is:
e: Full cost equals prime cost Rs 1,40,000 + shop on-cost Rs 35,000 + general on-cost Rs 15,000 + proforma on-cost Rs 10,000 = Rs 2,00,000.

q: On the day of disbursement of wages in a workshop, the amounts which could not be paid because the workers concerned were absent are:

options.A: Retained by the chargeman for payment on the following day
options.B: Returned and held under the Unpaid Wages head, to be claimed and paid later in the prescribed manner
options.C: Credited at once to the revenue of the railway
options.D: Distributed among the workers present on that day

e: Wages that could not be disbursed because workers were absent are returned and held under the Unpaid Wages head. They are paid later in the prescribed manner when claimed.

q: Rolling stock of a railway due for Periodic Overhaul is sent to a workshop of another railway because the home workshop has no spare capacity in the programme period. The cost of the overhaul is compiled by the workshop which executes it and is:

options.A: Borne finally by the executing railway as its own revenue expenditure
options.B: Charged to the Capital head of the executing railway
options.C: Recovered from the home railway through a transfer transaction, the home railway bearing the cost of overhaul of its own stock
options.D: Written off under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense of the executing workshop

e: The executing workshop compiles the overhaul cost, but the home railway bears the cost of overhauling its own stock. Recovery is made from the home railway through a transfer transaction.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, first-aid boxes or cupboards, equipped with the prescribed contents, are required to be provided and maintained in a factory at the rate of at least:

options.A: One for every 500 workers ordinarily employed
options.B: One for every 150 workers ordinarily employed
options.C: One for the factory as a whole, irrespective of the number of workers
options.D: One for every 1,000 workers ordinarily employed

e: Section 45 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires first-aid boxes or cupboards with prescribed contents at the rate of at least one for every 150 workers ordinarily employed in the factory.

q: In a foundry process, 1,000 kg of metal is charged into the process at a total process cost of Rs 45,000. The normal loss in the process is 10 per cent of the input and the actual good output is 920 kg. The cost per kg of good output, the normal loss being borne by the good output, is:
e: Normal loss is 10 per cent of 1,000 kg = 100 kg, so expected good output is 900 kg. Cost per kg of good output is Rs 45,000 / 900 = Rs 50, the normal loss being borne by good output.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Normal loss inherent in a workshop process is borne by the good output of the process, whose unit cost is worked out after providing for the normal loss.
2. Abnormal loss in a process is valued at the rate of the good output and taken out of the process cost, so that the unit cost of the normal output is not distorted by an avoidable loss.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Normal process loss is inherent and is borne by good output in its unit cost. Abnormal loss is valued at the good output rate and removed from process cost so normal unit cost is not distorted. Both statements are correct.

q: A job under execution in one shop of a workshop is sent to another shop of the same workshop for one operation and then returns to the first shop. The labour booked on the job in the second shop is:

options.A: Charged to a fresh manufacture job opened in the second shop
options.B: Booked to the same work order of the job, the cost following the job through whichever shop works on it
options.C: Charged to the shop on-cost of the second shop
options.D: Recovered from the first shop in cash

e: Cost follows the job. Labour done on a job in a second shop of the same workshop is booked to the same work order, not to a fresh job or to that shop's on-cost.

q: Material was drawn from stores for a manufacture job, but the job is cancelled by the indenting unit before any work is done on the material. The material, which is still unused in the shop, is:

options.A: Returned to the stores depot and credited to the job, so that no material cost remains charged against the cancelled job under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.B: Retained in the shop for use on any other job without any accounting adjustment
options.C: Sold as scrap by the shop
options.D: Charged to shop on-cost, the job having been cancelled

e: Unused material drawn for a job cancelled before any work is returned to the stores depot and credited to the job. No material cost then remains against the cancelled job in Workshop Manufacturing Suspense.

q: At the monthly closing of workshop accounts, the total of the balances on the in-progress folios of the Workshop General Register exceeds the balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense in the general books. The difference indicates that:

options.A: The outturn of the month has been overstated by the shops
options.B: The wages of the month have been overpaid
options.C: Some labour, stores or transfer items have not been posted on one side or the other, and the difference has to be traced and reconciled before the balance can be accepted as proved
options.D: The on-cost rates of the shops require revision

e: Job folios in the Workshop General Register must agree in total with Workshop Manufacturing Suspense in the general books. An excess means items are unposted on one side and must be traced and reconciled.

q: A railway workshop is asked to execute a job by a private person for his personal use. The correct position is that:

options.A: Such work is a normal part of workshop outturn and is billed at prime cost
options.B: Such work is charged to the revenue standing work order of the shop
options.C: The cost of such work is borne by the railway as a staff welfare measure
options.D: Private work of this kind is not ordinarily undertaken in a railway workshop; where it is exceptionally permitted under competent sanction, the full cost together with the prescribed charges is recovered

e: Private personal work is not ordinarily undertaken in a railway workshop. If exceptionally permitted under competent sanction, its full cost plus prescribed charges must be recovered from the person.

q: An article manufactured in a workshop at a material cost of Rs 30,000, labour of Rs 20,000 and on-cost of Rs 10,000 is transferred to the stores depot for stocking. The value at which it is taken into stores stock is:
e: Value taken into stores stock is the full manufacturing cost: material Rs 30,000 + labour Rs 20,000 + on-cost Rs 10,000 = Rs 60,000.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The on-cost estimates of a workshop are framed shop-wise for shop on-cost and for the workshop as a whole for general on-cost.
2. At the periodical review, the on-cost actually incurred is compared shop-wise with the estimates, so that shops in which on-cost is running high can be identified for control.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: On-cost estimates are framed shop-wise for shop on-cost and workshop-wise for general on-cost, and actuals are compared shop-wise with estimates at review to identify high on-cost shops. Both statements are correct.

q: For a workshop job, the standard rate of wages is Rs 55 per hour and the actual rate paid is Rs 60 per hour. The hours actually worked on the job are 300. The labour rate variance on the job is:

options.A: Rs 1,500 favourable
options.B: Rs 3,000 adverse
options.C: Rs 3,000 favourable
options.D: Rs 1,500 adverse

e: Labour rate variance equals (standard rate - actual rate) x actual hours = (Rs 55 - Rs 60) x 300 = Rs 1,500 adverse, since the actual rate exceeds the standard rate.

q: The bin cards maintained in the stores depot attached to a workshop record, for each item of stores:

options.A: The value of receipts and issues only
options.B: The quantities received, issued and in balance, without values, the value account being kept in the priced stores ledger
options.C: The names of the shops to which issues were made
options.D: The work orders on which the material was consumed

e: Bin cards in the stores depot record only quantities received, issued and in balance for each item. Values are kept separately in the priced stores ledger maintained by Accounts.

q: A manufacture job was completed and its outturn transferred in March. Surplus material drawn for the job is returned to stores in April, after the job folio has been closed. The credit for the returned material is:

options.A: Ignored, since the job is already closed
options.B: Credited to shop on-cost of April
options.C: Adjusted, through a transfer entry in April, to the same final head to which the outturn of the job was transferred, so that the head ultimately bears only the net cost
options.D: Credited to the earnings of the workshop

e: Surplus material returned after a job is closed is adjusted by transfer entry to the same final head that received the outturn. That head then ultimately bears only the net cost of the job.

q: The standing charges of a machine for a month are Rs 18,000 and its running charges for the month are Rs 12,000. The machine worked 1,500 hours in the month. The machine-hour rate of the machine is:

options.A: Rs 20 per hour
options.B: Rs 12 per hour
options.C: Rs 8 per hour
options.D: Rs 30 per hour

e: Machine-hour rate equals (standing charges Rs 18,000 + running charges Rs 12,000) / 1,500 hours worked = Rs 30,000 / 1,500 = Rs 20 per hour.

q: The Production Control Organisation of a workshop is responsible, on the executive side, mainly for:

options.A: Compiling the cost of jobs from the labour and stores abstracts
options.B: Passing the bills of the workshop for payment
options.C: Maintaining the priced stores ledger of the depot
options.D: Scheduling and progressing jobs through the shops so that the programmed outturn is achieved in time

e: The Production Control Organisation is an executive function for scheduling and progressing jobs through the shops so the programmed outturn is achieved in time, not for compiling costs or passing bills.

q: Under the unit-exchange system followed in the overhaul of rolling stock, a defective assembly removed from a unit under overhaul is:

options.A: Charged in full, at the price of a new assembly, to the unit from which it was removed
options.B: Sent for repair and returned to the pool of serviced assemblies, the unit under overhaul being fitted with a serviced assembly from the pool and bearing the value of the assembly so fitted
options.C: Sold as scrap immediately on removal
options.D: Retained by the shop as its own stock without any accounting entry

e: Under unit exchange, the unit under overhaul is fitted with a serviced assembly from the pool and bears its value. The defective assembly removed goes for repair and returns to the serviced pool.

q: Material of 500 kg was issued to a workshop job at Rs 40 per kg. On completion of the job, 80 kg of the material is returned to stores as surplus. The net material cost borne by the job is:
e: Material issued is 500 kg x Rs 40 = Rs 20,000. Surplus returned is 80 kg x Rs 40 = Rs 3,200 credited to the job, so net material cost is Rs 20,000 - Rs 3,200 = Rs 16,800.

q: Petty urgent purchases of consumable stores for a shop, of very small value, are made out of the standing cash imprest of the workshop. The imprest is recouped:

options.A: Out of the wages bills of the shop
options.B: By the chargeman out of the collections of the shop
options.C: By debiting the amount to Workshop Manufacturing Suspense permanently
options.D: On the basis of vouchers for the payments made, which are passed by the Accounts office and adjusted to the proper heads

e: Petty purchases from the workshop's standing cash imprest are recouped on vouchers for payments made, passed by the Accounts office and adjusted to the proper heads of account.

q: A machine recorded in the Plant Register of a workshop is transferred permanently to another workshop of the same railway. In the books of the transferring workshop, the correct treatment is to:

options.A: Remove the machine from its Plant Register through a transfer transaction in favour of the receiving workshop, so that its register continues to agree with the Block Account
options.B: Retain the machine in its Plant Register, since both workshops belong to the same railway
options.C: Write off the machine to shop on-cost
options.D: Show the machine as sold and credit the proceeds to revenue

e: A machine permanently transferred is removed from the transferring workshop's Plant Register through a transfer transaction in favour of the receiving workshop, keeping the register in agreement with the Block Account.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a creche is required to be provided and maintained in a factory in which the number of women workers ordinarily employed is:

options.A: More than 100
options.B: More than 30
options.C: More than 250
options.D: More than 500

e: Section 48 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires a creche in a factory where more than 30 women workers are ordinarily employed, for use of their children below the prescribed age.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, the register which the occupier of a factory is required to maintain, showing the name and nature of work of every adult worker, and which must be available to the Inspector during working hours, is the:

options.A: Register of leave with wages
options.B: Register of fines
options.C: Register of adult workers
options.D: Register of accidents

e: Section 62 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires the occupier to maintain a register of adult workers showing each worker's name and nature of work, available to the Inspector during working hours.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Productivity Linked Bonus paid to workshop staff forms part of the labour cost booked on individual jobs in the workshop.
2. The incentive bonus earned by workshop staff is an establishment charge which is never booked to jobs.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Neither statement is correct: Productivity Linked Bonus is not booked as direct labour on individual jobs, and incentive bonus of direct workers is in fact booked to jobs, not treated as a charge never booked to jobs.

q: The general on-cost of a workshop for a period is Rs 2,40,000 and is apportioned among the shops on the basis of direct labour. The direct labour of all shops totals Rs 24,00,000, of which one shop accounts for Rs 6,00,000. The share of general on-cost apportioned to that shop is:
e: The shop's share is Rs 2,40,000 x (Rs 6,00,000 / Rs 24,00,000) = Rs 2,40,000 x one-fourth = Rs 60,000, general on-cost being apportioned on the basis of direct labour.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where a job passes through two shops of a workshop, the on-cost absorbed on the job in each shop is at the rate of the shop in which the work was actually done.
2. The entire on-cost of a multi-shop job is absorbed in the finishing shop alone, at that shop's rate.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Each shop's on-cost is absorbed at that shop's own rate for work actually done there. A multi-shop job therefore bears on-cost shop-wise, not wholly at the finishing shop's rate; statement 1 alone is correct.

q: A new machine received in a workshop is erected and given trial runs before it is commissioned for regular work. The cost of the trial runs, incurred before commissioning, is:

options.A: Treated as part of the capital cost of the machine, being expenditure incurred in bringing it into working condition
options.B: Charged to shop on-cost of the month of the trial
options.C: Charged to the first job executed on the machine
options.D: Written off to the revenue of the railway as a loss

e: Trial runs before commissioning are expenditure incurred to bring the machine into working condition. Such pre-commissioning cost forms part of the capital cost of the machine.

q: Workshop staff are employed full-time on the erection of a machine sanctioned under the Machinery and Plant Programme. The wages of the staff for the period of erection are:

options.A: Charged to shop on-cost of the shop in which the machine is erected
options.B: Charged to the capital job for the erection of the machine, on which the installation cost is being compiled
options.C: Charged to the revenue standing work order of the shop
options.D: Held under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense as an unallocated charge

e: Staff employed full-time on erection of a Machinery and Plant Programme machine are charged to the capital erection job on which installation cost is compiled, not to shop on-cost or a revenue standing order.

q: On a workshop job, the material cost booked is Rs 1,00,000. Scrap arising on the job is returned to stores at an assessed value of Rs 6,000 and serviceable released material is credited to the job at Rs 9,000. The net material cost borne by the job is:
e: Net material cost equals material booked Rs 1,00,000 minus scrap credited Rs 6,000 and serviceable released material credited Rs 9,000, that is Rs 1,00,000 - Rs 15,000 = Rs 85,000.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Material issued from the stores depot to workshop jobs is priced at the issue rates of the priced stores ledger, and the difference between the issue value and the actual cost of the material is dealt with through the Stock Adjustment Account.
2. Such price differences are loaded on the individual jobs to which the material was issued.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Depot issues are priced at priced stores ledger issue rates, and the difference between issue value and actual cost goes through the Stock Adjustment Account, not onto individual jobs; statement 1 alone is correct.

q: Charges paid to an outside inspection agency for the inspection of a specific consignment of material purchased for a workshop are treated in costing as:

options.A: Part of the general on-cost of the workshop
options.B: A charge on the shop which will use the material
options.C: A deduction from the wages of the stores staff
options.D: Part of the cost of that material, being an expense incurred directly in acquiring it

e: Inspection charges paid for a specific consignment are a direct expense of acquiring that material. They therefore form part of the cost of that material, not general on-cost.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Objections raised in internal check or audit on workshop expenditure are pursued by the Workshop Accounts Office with the executive until they are settled or regularised under competent orders.
2. Amounts held under objection in workshop accounts are automatically written off at the close of the financial year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Objections from internal check or audit must be pursued with the executive until settled or regularised under competent orders. They are never automatically written off at year end; statement 1 alone is correct.

q: During verification of the material lying in a shop, an excess is found over the quantities drawn for jobs and awaiting accountal. Pending investigation, the correct course is to:

options.A: Allow the shop to retain the excess without any record
options.B: Sell the excess material and credit the proceeds to the Staff Benefit Fund
options.C: Charge the value of the excess to the last job executed in the shop
options.D: Take the excess into account under objection/suspense and adjust it, after investigation, under the orders of the competent authority

e: Excess material found in a shop pending investigation is taken into account under objection or suspense. After investigation it is adjusted under orders of the competent authority, not retained without record.

q: Shop A has on-cost of Rs 45,000 on direct labour of Rs 1,50,000, and Shop B has on-cost of Rs 80,000 on direct labour of Rs 2,00,000. A job executed in Shop B has direct labour of Rs 25,000. The on-cost absorbed on the job is:
e: Shop B's on-cost rate is Rs 80,000 / Rs 2,00,000 = 40 per cent of direct labour. On a Shop B job with direct labour Rs 25,000, absorbed on-cost is 40 per cent x Rs 25,000 = Rs 10,000.

q: Material purchased for a workshop is received in its attached stores depot. Before the material can be issued to jobs, the regular course is that it is:

options.A: Taken into the depot's receipt records and the priced stores ledger, issues to jobs being made thereafter against requisitions
options.B: Delivered directly to the shops, the depot records being made at the end of the year
options.C: Held under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense as a completed job
options.D: Accounted for only in the Plant Register of the workshop

e: Purchased material is first taken into the depot's receipt records and the priced stores ledger. Only thereafter is it issued to jobs against requisitions, ensuring stock accountal before use.

q: A manufacture job is completed, but the indenting unit refuses to accept the article because it deviates from the specification given by it, the deviation being attributable to the workshop. Until the article is rectified and accepted, or otherwise disposed of under competent orders, its cost:

options.A: Is transferred at once to the final head of the indenting unit
options.B: Is written off to the revenue of the workshop
options.C: Is charged to the shop on-cost of the shops which made it
options.D: Remains under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense against the job, pending rectification or disposal

e: An article refused for a workshop-caused deviation cannot be transferred to the indenting unit or written off. Its cost remains under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense pending rectification or disposal under competent orders.

q: A debit balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense at the end of a month indicates that:

options.A: The cost accumulated on jobs in hand and not yet transferred out exceeds the cost transferred out of the suspense up to that date
options.B: The workshop has earned a profit on the jobs completed during the month
options.C: Stores have been issued to jobs in excess of the sanctioned estimates
options.D: Wages paid in the workshop exceed the budget allotment of the workshop

e: A debit balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense means cost accumulated on jobs in hand and not yet transferred out exceeds cost transferred out to date - in short, the value of work in progress.

q: When an article manufactured in a workshop is transferred to the stores depot for stocking, the accounting effect in the workshop books is that:

options.A: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is debited and Stores Suspense is credited
options.B: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is credited and the stores stock account is debited with the cost of the article
options.C: The cost of the article is written off to the revenue of the workshop
options.D: No entry is passed, since both the workshop and the depot belong to the same railway

e: Transfer to stores stock credits Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, which held the manufacturing cost, and debits the stores stock account with the article's cost, moving it from manufacture to stock.

q: The labour distribution statement compiled in a Workshop Accounts Office from the job cards and tally sheets shows:

options.A: The names of the workers who were absent during the month
options.B: The total wages payable to each worker of the workshop
options.C: The distribution of the wages of workshop staff over the several work orders on which they were employed during the period
options.D: The incentive bonus payable to each shop of the workshop

e: The labour distribution statement, compiled from job cards and tally sheets, shows how wages of workshop staff are distributed over the several work orders on which they were employed during the period.

q: The material abstract prepared in connection with workshop jobs summarises:

options.A: The quantities of stores held in balance in the stores depot
options.B: The purchases of stores made by the workshop during the month
options.C: The scrap generated in the shops during the period
options.D: The value of stores issued from the depot against the several work orders during the period

e: The material abstract summarises the value of stores issued from the depot against the several work orders during the period, providing the posting basis for material debits to jobs.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The cost booked on jobs which remain incomplete at the close of a financial year continues to lie under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense.
2. Such cost is charged to the final Revenue or Capital head at the close of that year itself, even though the jobs are incomplete.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Cost on jobs incomplete at the close of a financial year continues to lie under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense. It is charged to the final head only on transfer of outturn; statement 1 alone is correct.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, an adult worker in a factory is not ordinarily permitted to work for more than:

options.A: 36 hours in a week
options.B: 60 hours in a week
options.C: 48 hours in a week
options.D: 72 hours in a week

e: Section 51 of the Factories Act, 1948 provides that no adult worker shall ordinarily be required or allowed to work in a factory for more than 48 hours in any week.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, the period of work of an adult worker in a factory is so arranged that no period of work exceeds five hours without an interval for rest of at least:

options.A: Fifteen minutes
options.B: Half an hour
options.C: One hour
options.D: Two hours

e: Section 55 of the Factories Act, 1948 requires work periods to be arranged so that no period exceeds five hours without an interval for rest of at least half an hour.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, where a worker in a factory works for more than nine hours in a day or more than forty-eight hours in a week, he is entitled, in respect of the overtime work, to wages at:

options.A: The ordinary rate of wages
options.B: One and a half times the ordinary rate of wages
options.C: Three times the ordinary rate of wages
options.D: Twice the ordinary rate of wages

e: Section 59 of the Factories Act, 1948 entitles a worker who works over nine hours a day or over 48 hours a week to overtime wages at twice the ordinary rate of wages.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, an adult worker in a factory who has worked for the prescribed qualifying period earns leave with wages at the rate of:

options.A: One day for every ten days of work performed in the previous calendar year
options.B: One day for every twenty days of work performed in the previous calendar year
options.C: One day for every thirty days of work performed in the previous calendar year
options.D: One day for every fifteen days of work performed in the previous calendar year

e: Section 79 of the Factories Act, 1948 gives an adult worker who has completed the qualifying period leave with wages at one day for every 20 days of work performed in the previous calendar year.

q: On a workshop job, the standard price of a material is Rs 50 per unit, the price actually paid is Rs 55 per unit and the quantity consumed is 2,000 units. The material price variance on the job is:

options.A: Rs 10,000 adverse
options.B: Rs 10,000 favourable
options.C: Rs 5,000 adverse
options.D: Rs 1,10,000 adverse

e: Material price variance equals (standard price - actual price) x quantity consumed = (Rs 50 - Rs 55) x 2,000 = Rs 10,000 adverse, since the price paid exceeds the standard price.
